q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT DISTINCT f1.drinker AS drinkerA, f2.drinker AS drinkerB FROM frequents AS f1, frequents AS f2 WHERE f1.bar = f2.bar AND f1.drinker > f2.drinker AND f1.times_a_week = f2.times_a_week

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 compares the total times a week each drinker frequents any bar, while Q2 compares the times a week each drinker frequents a specific bar.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are two drinkers who frequent the same bar the same number of times a week, but different bars. Q1 will return both drinkers, while Q2 will not return any results.
